Meeting Header
Date: 2028-09-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (QuantumBridge - CTO), Marco Silva (QuantumBridge - Lead ML Engineer), Aisha Khan (QuantumBridge - Platform Engineer)

Auto-generated summary: (see summary field)

[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're Ethan and Priya from Redwood, how are you all?
[00:06] Lena (QuantumBridge - CTO): Doing well, thanks. Excited to chat, we've been digging into open models and where they fit in our stack.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda — we want to understand your workloads (latency, tokens, languages), any compliance constraints, and then sketch a model and deployment path. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:26] Marco (QuantumBridge): Cool. High level — our main product uses long-doc retrieval and summarization for research analysts, so context length is a big deal. We're seeing docs of 200k characters, so approximating we need 32k token windows or ability to stitch with KV caching.
[00:41] Aisha (QuantumBridge): Also multilingual — Spanish and Portuguese first, then Mandarin later. And we need tool-calling for database lookups and calling internal microservices safely.
[00:51] Ethan (Redwood AE): Solid. So two dimensions — model capability/context and infra. Do you have an initial latency SLO and cost sensitivity?
[00:58] Lena: Latency — for interactive analyst flows we'd like p95 < 400ms ideally, but we can tolerate up to 800ms for heavier summarization. Cost wise we care about unit token cost; we're not at infinite budget but prefer predictable pricing with reserved capacity for production.
[01:14] Priya: Ok that points toward Dedicated if predictability and low p95 are priorities, but Hosted can be a fast way to prototype. Private (VPC or on-prem) is for strict data residency and when you need customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[01:28] Marco: On models, we've benchmarked a few open families — MPT variants, LlamaX-xxl-ish forks, and a couple of 32k-capable models. The tradeoffs are accuracy on long-context summarization and the ability to support tool calls and structured outputs.
[01:42] Ethan: Right. One practical approach is hybrid: start with Hosted for a pilot using a 32k open model that Redwood has validated, run a lightweight benchmark (latency + ROUGE/BLEU-ish quality metrics), then move to Dedicated with quantization and batching tuned for your throughput.
[01:56] Marco: How does KV cache work across sessions? We have repeated context prefixes — hopping between user sessions.
[02:02] Priya: Our runtime supports prefix KV caching and cross-request reuse when policy allows. For multi-tenant workloads we'd isolate by customer; for your case, you can configure cache TTLs and mutexes. We also do automatic batching but it respects latency SLOs.
[02:19] Lena: Security — we need SOC 2 Type II, SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs, and optional HSM support for keys. Also data retention policies — some records must be purged within 30 days.
[02:30] Ethan: We can share SOC2/ISO docs; Redwood Hosted is SOC2-compliant, Dedicated and Private give you more control over KMS and retention. For HSM integrations we support customer-managed keys via KMS APIs and can integrate with onboarded HSMs in Private deployments.
[02:46] Aisha: If we run Dedicated, is it possible to have VPC peering and egress controls? And how about on-prem air-gapped later?
[02:54] Priya: Yes on Dedicated you can have VPC peering, control egress, and restrict management plane traffic. Private on-prem is our lane for air-gapped setups but it's a heavier lift and generally requires a licensing agreement.
[03:06] Marco: Model quantization concerns — for long-context, does 4-bit or 8-bit quantization hurt summarization quality?
[03:12] Priya: There's a model-dependent curve. Some newer LlamaX-like models maintain quality at 4-bit (QLoRA-style) for many tasks, but for chain-of-thought or delicate abstraction tasks you might see regressions. Our Optimize tooling recommends quantization profiles by workload; we can run A/B quality checks during the PoC.
[03:29] Lena: Multilingual performance — we care about Spanish and Portuguese being first-class, not half-decent. Are there open models you'd recommend?
[03:36] Ethan: For Spanish/Portuguese, some community models fine-tuned on multilingual corpora do well — think models like LlamaX-multi, MPT-xxl-multi, or Meta derivatives. Redwood has curated performance profiles — we'll send a short list with sample evals.
[03:50] Marco: Tool-calling — we need structured function calls and the ability to surface retrieval results safely. Can Redwood runtime enforce allow-lists and sanitization before invoking internal services?
[03:59] Priya: Yes, we support tool-calling primitives and an execution sandbox pattern. You can define allowed endpoints, rate limits, and pre/post hooks for sanitization. For retrieval we integrate with vector stores and you can control what result chunks are returned to the model.
[04:14] Aisha: About telemetry — we need token-level cost breakdown, per-call latencies, and trace ids to attach to our logs.
[04:20] Ethan: That's in Redwood Console — token-level cost, per-route dashboards, trace ids, and exportable logs for your SIEM. You can also set alerting for quality regressions tied to prompt sets.
[04:33] Lena: If we do a PoC, what's realistic to measure in two weeks?
[04:37] Priya: Two weeks is enough for a hosted pilot: share a representative sample of docs (sanitized), we run 32k context passes plus a shorter cached run, measure latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, and a qualitative eval on summaries. For dedicated benchmarking we recommend 4–6 weeks because of infra sizing and tuning.
[04:55] Marco: Are there any known gotchas with function-calling across token-limited models? We've seen truncation of structured outputs.
[05:03] Priya: Truncation can happen if responses exceed context or buffer sizes. We support structured output enforcement via output schemas and streaming; streaming helps with large outputs and reduces perceived latency. Also recommend chunking for very large results and issuing follow-up calls for subsequent pages.
[05:20] Ethan: Quick objection we often hear — "why not just self-host open models?" The answer is tradeoffs: you own everything but you also own infra ops, kernel optimizations, quantization tuning, and SLO guarantees. Redwood tries to give you the ops backbone plus best-practice kernels so teams can focus on product.
[05:39] Lena: Pricewise — show us hosted pilot cost vs dedicated reserved monthly. We'll map against our expected queries per second.
[05:46] Ethan: Will do. We'll include a TCO calc that factors in quantization gains and batching policies.
[05:52] (brief cross-talk)
[05:54] Aisha: For the PoC dataset, do you need raw docs or embeddings?
[05:58] Priya: Raw docs preferred; we'll run ingestion and produce embeddings as part of the PoC. If you already have vector DB snapshots, that helps us skip indexing time.
[06:08] Marco: One more thing — do you support multilingual tokenization differences? We had issues where tokenizers split Spanish contractions oddly.
[06:15] Priya: Tokenizer behavior is model-specific; part of our model curation includes tokenizer checks. We'll flag any tokenization anomalies in the PoC report.
[06:25] Ethan: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[06:28] (06:28) Recap
[06:30] Ethan: Action items: I'll send pricing matrix and a short model recommendation list. Priya will draft a PoC plan focusing on 32k context, multilingual test cases, and tool-calling test harness. Aisha will share sanitised sample docs and any vector DB access notes. Lena will confirm timelines internally and identify legal/security contacts for SOC2/ISO docs.
[06:52] Lena: Sounds good. We may want an additional technical deep dive for on-prem options — if air-gapped is on the table we'll get legal involved.
[06:59] Ethan: We'll schedule that once you confirm. Thanks everyone.
[07:02] Marco: Thanks, appreciate it.
